claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic, as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a single-phase BCC structure.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and undergoes pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
A thin alumina-based or silicide coating will significantly improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed coating will not compromise the alloy's room- or elevated-temperature mechanical performance.
The coating will form a continuous, dense, and adherent alumina or silicide surface scale.
The surface scale will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
Impeded oxygen diffusion will reduce oxygen uptake by the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Reduced oxygen uptake will prevent pesting and oxidation-induced degradation.
Preventing oxidation-induced degradation will preserve the substrate microstructure responsible for strength and ductility.
Relative to uncoated material, coated samples will show lower oxidation mass gain.
Relative to uncoated material, coated samples will show less pronounced oxide-scale formation.
Relative to uncoated material, coated samples will retain room- and high-temperature yield strength and ductility.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr deteriorates through rapid oxidation in high-temperature air.
Oxidation of untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undermines its mechanical performance.
The coating is expected to remain effective in air up to approximately 1000 °C for exposures around 5 hours and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Making the coating sufficiently thin will avoid altering the alloy's bulk mechanical response.
